01-title-mode-menu.verdict: The new title menu loses the three boxed cards and gains a Settings button, but it is still a long, crowded stack of explaining sentences and equal-weight buttons that reads like a web form, not an ARC Raiders-grade title screen.

02-welcome-pack.verdict: A full-screen dark slab with a tiny left-hugging list, a wall of explaining text and a huge dead void; it reads as a debug dump rather than a welcome reward moment, with no hierarchy and no celebration.

03-hub-floor.verdict: The hub reads as a prototype: the eight same-size station labels compete with each other, the HUD text is tiny and pushed into the corners, and the bottom of the screen is cluttered with a hotbar, a toast and a hint line.

04-stash-terminal.verdict: A dense, cluttered stash screen with no clear focal point, tiny low-contrast labels and several stacked instruction and explanation strips; it reads as a debug tool, not a polished extraction-shooter menu.

05-sector-page.verdict: A dense, form-like pre-raid screen where a half-empty brown banner with a tiny map, rows of identical amber chips and three explanatory paragraphs bury the one decision that matters, so it reads as a debug panel rather than a polished menu.

06-terms.verdict: A tidy but flat, generic dark modal with no focal point, no visible pad focus, a wordy intro paragraph, and footer buttons that break the content margins, so it reads as a debug list rather than a game contract screen.

07-party-coop.verdict: A text-heavy modal that reads as a generic dark template: two paragraphs of explaining copy swamp the actual choice (host or join), the controls are tiny and misaligned, and there is no pad focus or party-slot UI.

08-shop.verdict: A clean dark grid with a good gold selection state, but the bottom half of the screen is empty, the cream detail panel clashes with the dark UI, and the currency header, tiny type, and flavor text undercut the polish.

09-craft.verdict: The craft grid is clean and readable, but the screen is a top-heavy template with a dead lower half, a cream detail card that clashes with the dark UI, and a header that collides and shows redundant currency.

10-hire.verdict: A tidy but generic grid, undermined by a loud red glitch banner that outranks everything, a washed-out cream detail panel with a disabled-looking Hire button, and duplicated currency and price data.

11-wirt-gambler.verdict: A tidy but generic dark modal with no focal point: the title, two competing boxes and a pile of explanatory text all sit at similar weight, and the buttons look disabled and have no visible pad focus.

12-mainframe-contracts.verdict: A functional but generic dark list-and-detail template: the cream detail card clashes with the dark UI, the header currency cluster collides, every row looks identical, and there is placeholder copy and leftover clutter.

14-mainframe-racks.verdict: A flat, text-heavy dark form with placeholder profanity on screen, disabled buttons that read as dead rectangles, a collision in the header currency block, and nothing to draw the eye, so it is far below the polish bar.

16-bar-last-pour.verdict: A clean but generic dark modal with a mismatched centered title, two identical yellow buttons that flatten hierarchy, no visible pad focus, and a lot of dead space.

17-fashion-mirror.verdict: A competent dark-panel template with a clear two-column layout, but the grid is a wall of near-identical tiles, the operator preview is dwarfed, and the header, footer and list clip or crowd, so it reads as a debug inventory and not a Fortnite-grade fashion screen.

18-settings-hub.verdict: A dense, flat settings list with two competing tab rows, a duplicated detail panel and a wasted right half, so it reads as a debug form rather than a polished AAA settings screen.

19-raid-hud-drop-first-raid.verdict: The raid HUD is functional but cluttered: five or six competing text panels, a keybind cheat sheet that stays open, duplicated tooltips and tiny dense type leave no clear focal point and no consistent panel language.

21-raid-hud-calm.verdict: The new version trims the run-info contract list and tones down the credits and backpack hint, but the HUD is still a pile of small, equal-weight dark boxes with tiny text, dollar signs, a clipped minimap label and a title-case 'Run Info' that breaks the sentence-case rule.

22-raid-map-open.verdict: The map is readable as a data dump, but labels collide with icons and with each other, the zone names are almost invisible, and the frame, header and HUD have no shared system, so it looks like a debug overlay rather than a polished AAA map.

23-raid-backpack-open.verdict: The backpack is a wide, mostly empty dark slab with tiny, low-contrast text and three lonely item slots, and it sits in a HUD cluttered with competing text blocks, so it looks like a debug panel rather than a AAA inventory.

25-raid-pause-box.verdict: The pause menu is serviceable, with a clear primary button and a sentence-case title, but a dense five-row keybind wall, an apologetic feedback sentence and a barely dimmed HUD bleeding through make it look like a debug overlay rather than a polished AAA pause screen.

26-settings-from-pause-top.verdict: A dense, flat, low-contrast settings dump with duplicate tab rows, tiny text and a mostly empty detail panel; it works as a template but has no hierarchy or game identity.

32-keys-window.verdict: A functional but flat, spreadsheet-like rebind table with two explaining sentences, weak hierarchy, ghosted Rebind buttons, a lopsided layout and no visible focus state, so it reads as a generic template rather than a polished PILLAGERS screen.

33-raid-fight-alerts.verdict: The HUD works as a debug-style overlay but feels like a pile of mismatched panels: the minimap is clipped and overlaps a zone label, the contracts list is dense with tiny text, and the alert is duplicated three times.

35-kia-card.verdict: The death card has a clear red title and a single yellow primary button, but the stacked centered text, the tiny low-contrast lines, the 'Lost' repetition and the cluttered info above make it look like a debug dialog rather than a polished AAA screen.

38-extracted-card.verdict: The Extracted card has a clear title and a strong primary button, but it is a dense stack of small centered text lines with weak hierarchy, a muddy dimmed HUD behind it, and no pad focus cue.

40-whats-new-card.verdict: A full-width flat grey slab of repetitive changelog text slices through the middle of the hub, clipping the station labels and leaving the world HUD fighting it, so it reads as a debug dump and not a polished what's-new card.

45-arcade-attract-board.verdict: A sentence-case, centered attract screen with a clear title and prompt, but it sits on a flat black void with no art, an empty leaderboard, and a dim call to action, so it reads as a placeholder and not a game's front door.

50-arcade-hud-live.verdict: A busy, mismatched HUD where tiny, low-contrast text sits on a noisy map, the bottom-right panel overlaps the world and its own props, and the corners disagree on type, size and panel style.

52-arcade-run-over.verdict: A bare text-on-black end screen with a game title that outshouts the result, redundant score lines, a dim call to action, and no panel, art, or identity beyond the font.

57-title-2p-coop-picked.verdict: A competent dark-amber template with a clear title, but the screen is a crowded stack of explainer text, tutorial cards, a control legend, seven near-identical mode buttons, an error banner and a save form, so nothing leads the eye to the action and the style is inconsistent.

59-raid-abandon-confirm.verdict: A pause modal that doubles as a control cheat-sheet: the abandon confirmation is buried under five rows of keybind chips, a stray feedback sentence and mismatched button casing, while the HUD bleeding through behind the scrim adds noise.

65-codex.verdict: A legible but sparse card grid that fills only the top third of the screen, leaving a huge dead void, with a weak title, a jammed header, and no visible focus state.

66-trophy-case.verdict: The trophy cards are tidy individually, but the screen is two-thirds empty, the grid orphans a single card on row two, nothing shows focus, and the header stats and toast are crude.

62-arcade-operator-menu.verdict: A small, bright operator modal sits on top of a dimmed attract screen whose title, scoreboard and 'Press any button' prompt are still visible and compete with it, so the layering is muddled and the modal is tiny for a 1080 couch view.

61-raid-wheel-open.verdict: The wheel itself has a clear gold focus segment, but it is buried under a controls cheat-sheet that overlaps it, a minimap and contracts list that clip, and a dozen competing HUD panels with inconsistent type and no shared panel style.

58-coop-player2-window-title.verdict: The title screen has a clear gold CTA and a decent logo, but it is a stack of small centered text, tutorial cards, a keybind strip and an orange paragraph of explanation, so the hierarchy is muddy and the screen reads like a web form rather than a game menu.

46-arcade-attract-how-to-play.verdict: A clean, legible black-screen controls table with a consistent amber and bone palette, but it is flat, generic and visually unfinished: the "Press any button" prompt outweighs the content, the table has no structure, and nothing says extraction shooter.

37-raid-extracting-countdown.verdict: The HUD is overloaded: a controls cheat-sheet, contracts list, scoreboard, pickup toasts, and a backpack panel all compete at once, with mismatched type sizes, overlapping labels, and no clear first read.

77-haul-reveal-done.verdict: A centered modal with a nice teal title and a clear primary button, but the body is a long stack of small centered text lines with explaining sentences, weak hierarchy between the loot and the stats, and a cluttered HUD bleeding through behind it.
